title: Gate Forty-One
mood: flirty and unhurried, hoping the delay gets longer
subject: sharing one phone charger with a stranger at an airport gate during a five-hour delay
caption: Amapiano pop in the 2025 South African crossover style. A pitched log-drum bass that glides between notes and plays the whole bassline; a sparse kick that skips beats; shakers and syncopated open hi-hats carrying the groove; jazzy Rhodes chords in extended ninth voicings; a soft airy pad underneath. Dry and spacious with lots of air between the parts, the log drum and the voice forward. Female voice, breathy and laid-back R&B in the low-middle register, singing close to the mic, with her own soft harmony doubling the hook lines. 112 BPM, F minor. Flirty and unhurried, hoping the delay gets longer. No four-on-the-floor house kick, no afrobeats guitar, no trap hi-hats, no autotune, no sampled voice hooks, no EDM drop.
lyrics:
[Intro - log drum and Rhodes chords, short]

[Verse 1]
Gate forty-one and the board just turned red
Delayed till ten and my phone's on four percent
One plug by the window and you're sat on it
You hold up your cable and say we can take turns

[Pre-Chorus]
Twenty minutes yours, twenty minutes mine
You set a timer on your watch

[Chorus]
Don't board it yet, don't board it yet
I've got your charger and you've got half my fries
Twenty minutes yours, twenty minutes mine
Don't board it yet

[Verse 2]
Same flight, you're nine C and I'm thirty-two E
You say the middle seat next to you is free
The screen says delayed again till twelve
And I don't even sigh

[Pre-Chorus]
Your timer's gone off three times now
Neither of us moved the plug

[Chorus]
Don't board it yet, don't board it yet
I've got your charger and I've got your coat
Row nine, middle seat, if they'll let me move
Don't board it yet

[Instrumental Break - log drum solo with shakers]

[Outro - log drum alone, then Rhodes]
Now boarding, gate forty-one
You say keep the cable, see you in row nine
